full_judgment:
18. The learned Advocate Mr SM Monir appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner while taken this Court through the judgment passed by the Courts below draws the attention of this Court to the relevant findings of the appellate Court and argued that the impugned judgment passed in appeal below being a judgment of reversal, the learned appellate Court was duty bound to reverse the finding of the trial Court as to the genunity of the plaintiff's bainapatra executed by the defendant No. 1 Raja Kha on 2-4-1979 and since the learned Appellate Court failed to specifically and particularly reverse the findings of the trial Court the impugned judgment is liable to be interfered with by this Court. 

 20. The learned Advocate Mr SM Monir strenuously argued that the alleged bainapatra executed in favour of the defendant No. 3 is nothing but to defeat the right of the plaintiff to have the sell finalized in his favour and therefore the impugned judgment of reversal is bad in law which is required to be interfered with by this Court. 

 22. The learned Advocate Mr SM Monir further argued that as the impugned judgment is a judgment of reversal this Court is lawfully entitled to apprise the evidence on record in order to consider the contending claim of the parties and if this Court apprise the evidence on record it will be revealed that the plaintiff successfully proved his bainapatra dated 2-4-1979 by the PWs 2 and 3 who are natural and impartial witness to the said bainapatra while the defendant No. 3 failed to prove his so-called bainapatra dated 1-1-1979 which has been written in the white paper and if the two bainapatra dated 1-1-1979 and 2-4-1979 are taken side by side it will reveal that there is every possibility of creating a bainapatra by concoction written in a white paper rather than creating a bainapatra written on stamp paper. 2 

 28. The impugned judgment is a judgment of reversal having adverse finding as to the ability of the plaintiff to prove his case. The finding of the appellate Court and the findings of the trial Court below are diverse on the point of proving the plaintiff's case which prompted this Court to apprise the evidence on record independently for coming to the correct finding on the point. The trial Courts found the bainapatra dated 2-4-1979 allegedly by Raja Kha in favour of the plaintiff to be a genuine one. The bainapatra dated 1-1-1979 was written by Md Lutfor Rahman and attested by three witnesses namely Habibur Rahman Sheikh, Mohammad Kafiluddin Sheikh and Ansan Uddin Talukder. Out of these witnesses the plaintiff has examined Habibur Rahman Sheikh @ Mohammad Habibur Rahman and also the scribe Md Lutfor Rahman. These two witnesses proved the genunity of the plaintiff's bainapatra dated 2-4-1979 against which the defendant has taken the ground that witness Habibur Rahman is a close relation to the plaintiff. The learned Judge of the trial Court considered the evidence of PW 2 Lutfor Rahman and found that he has deposed that Raja Kha executed the bainapatra which he has written on 2-4-1979 in presence of Raja Kha and the witnesses of the said bainapatra had also signed the same in his presence. He has taken the signature of Raja Kha in the said bainapatra. The learned Judge of the trial Court found that this witness in his cross-examination has admitted that he was acquainted with the executants Raja Kha since long. It appears that the trial Court also considered the evidence of PW 3 Habibur Rahman despite the fact that he is a close relation of the plaintiff which has been admitted in the cross-examination. This witness also said that he was present at the time of execution of the bainapatra and he signed the bainapatra as an attesting witness. Therefore, it appears that the plaintiff witnesses have proved the fact that Raja Kha had executed the said bainapatra dated 2-4-1979.
